blocks.prompt: 11 If \(a, b, c, d\) are in H.P., show that \(3(a - b)(c - d) = (b - c)(a - d)\).
blocks.explanation:
A proof with four H.P. terms.
Their reciprocals form an A.P.; call its first term \(p\) and common difference \(q\).
Plan: write each difference like \(a - b\) in terms of \(p, q\), then compare both sides.
steps:
Given: \(a, b, c, d\) are in H.P.
To prove: \(3(a - b)(c - d) = (b - c)(a - d)\).
Method: \(\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{b}, \frac{1}{c}, \frac{1}{d}\) are in A.P., so
\[\dfrac{1}{a} = p, \; \dfrac{1}{b} = p + q\]
\[\dfrac{1}{c} = p + 2q, \; \dfrac{1}{d} = p + 3q\]
(all non-zero).

Express a difference of two terms
\[a - b = \dfrac{1}{p} - \dfrac{1}{p + q}\]
\[= \dfrac{q}{p(p + q)}\]
Why: Common denominator: \((p + q) - p = q\). In general, for any two terms, \(x - y = \frac{\frac{1}{y} - \frac{1}{x}}{\frac{1}{x} \cdot \frac{1}{y}}\).

The other three differences
\[c - d = \dfrac{q}{(p + 2q)(p + 3q)}\]
\[b - c = \dfrac{q}{(p + q)(p + 2q)}\]
\[a - d = \dfrac{3q}{p(p + 3q)}\]
Why: Same method; for \(a - d\) the reciprocals differ by \(3q\).

Left-hand side
\[3(a - b)(c - d)\]
\[= \dfrac{3q \cdot q}{p(p + q)(p + 2q)(p + 3q)}\]
\[= \dfrac{3q^{2}}{p(p + q)(p + 2q)(p + 3q)}\]
Why: Multiply the two fractions.

Right-hand side
\[(b - c)(a - d)\]
\[= \dfrac{q \cdot 3q}{(p + q)(p + 2q) \cdot p(p + 3q)}\]
\[= \dfrac{3q^{2}}{p(p + q)(p + 2q)(p + 3q)}\]
Why: Same four factors in the denominator, same top \(3q^{2}\).

Conclude
\[3(a - b)(c - d) = (b - c)(a - d)\]
Why: Both sides equal the same expression.

Check with numbers: \(a = 1, b = \frac{1}{2}, c = \frac{1}{3}, d = \frac{1}{4}\).
\[3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{1}{8}\]
\[\dfrac{1}{6} \cdot \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{1}{8} \;\checkmark\]
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(3(a - b)(c - d) = (b - c)(a - d)\).
